fields.everydayGoal: Roll a sheet of dough flat on a kitchen table.
fields.normalExpectation: Pressing a rolling pin against dough makes the dough thinner and spreads it across the tabletop.
fields.impossibleRule: WHEN the rolling pin presses down against dough, THE dough directly beneath its barrel ALWAYS thickens upward into a tall vertical wall supporting the barrel instead of flattening.
fields.visibleTrigger: Mimi presses both rolling-pin handles downward with the barrel in contact with the dough.
fields.whyThisObject: A rolling pin applies broad downward pressure specifically to flatten dough; the upward wall visibly contradicts that ordinary use at the barrel's contact surface.
fields.goalRuleRelationship: The pressure Mimi needs to flatten the dough instead makes the contacted dough taller, holding the rolling pin above the surrounding flat sheet.
fields.frameZeroDescription: Mimi stands behind a kitchen table, leaning forward with both palms pressing down on the handles of a horizontal rolling pin. A broad, thin sheet of dough lies on the tabletop. Directly beneath the rolling-pin barrel, that same sheet forms a smooth, chest-high vertical wall of dough, as wide as the barrel and only as thick as the barrel's contact strip. The barrel rests across the wall's narrow top, far above the flat dough on either side. Mimi's downward-braced arms and the towering dough wall form the large central silhouette against a plain kitchen background.

evidence.sourceText: Roll a sheet of dough flat on a kitchen table.
Pressing a rolling pin against dough makes the dough thinner and spreads it across the tabletop.
WHEN the rolling pin presses down against dough, THE dough directly beneath its barrel ALWAYS thickens upward into a tall vertical wall supporting the barrel instead of flattening.
Mimi presses both rolling-pin handles downward with the barrel in contact with the dough.

Mimi stands behind a kitchen table, leaning forward with both palms pressing down on the handles of a horizontal rolling pin. A broad, thin sheet of dough lies on the tabletop. Directly beneath the rolling-pin barrel, that same sheet forms a smooth, chest-high vertical wall of dough, as wide as the barrel and only as thick as the barrel's contact strip. The barrel rests across the wall's narrow top, far above the flat dough on either side. Mimi's downward-braced arms and the towering dough wall form the large central silhouette against a plain kitchen background.
A rolling pin applies broad downward pressure specifically to flatten dough; the upward wall visibly contradicts that ordinary use at the barrel's contact surface.
The pressure Mimi needs to flatten the dough instead makes the contacted dough taller, holding the rolling pin above the surrounding flat sheet.

Keep openingPhysicalState/goal/problem evidence as input context; do not change the physical state they describe. One canonical protagonist, one primary object, one location, one everyday goal, strange but intuitive. The same object-specific useful operation must directly obstruct the goal; never random portable magic.

Generate exactly 4 or 5 major causal beats including payoff: strategy/action -> visible consequence -> new information/state change. Beat 1 CONTINUES the exact state in frame zero, with no reset, normal setup or deferred first activation. State concrete trigger/contact, target, response and changed physical state; passive consequences must trace to existing activations. Use concise stageable sentences and readable pacing, no hidden sub-scenes or reworded retries. Vary strategy, position, leverage, timing, magnitude, accumulation, control, information, goal distance or environmental consequence. Environment is passive staging; avoid the default harder/two-hands/brace/fake-success ladder.

The opening rule's trigger -> target -> response is immutable in every beat. No second power, new material/function, changed target, direction, timing or agency, exception, actor loophole or reinterpretation. Spread, transfer and magnitude must already follow the same causal function. The strongest final visual state change must derive from it: surprising but inevitable, no unrelated finale behavior, rescue or explanatory realization. Describe BEFORE STATE -> SAME RULE ACTIVATION -> AFTER STATE with clear source/destination and directional reference frame; no reversible or ambiguous orientation. finalPayoff equals the last visibleConsequence exactly, with no extra event. Vary causal payoff shapes rather than force routine temporary-success/reset. A loop is optional; no reset magic.

The entire story reads with sound off; incidental OPTIONAL dialogue never explains the goal/rule/trigger/payoff. Broad poses, stable identities and silhouettes, few moving elements; avoid tiny text, many small objects, fine hand work/mechanics, crowds, rapid location changes and unstageable invisible forces. Child-safe comedy only: no injury, weapons, dangerous restraint or sexual content. Historical cautions are not templates; avoid routine chair inversion, adhesion, footwear resets, growth/shrink, generic reversal or escape variants. No certification of novelty.

Privately compare each beat and payoff to the frozen rule and opening. If preserving them is impossible, do not silently repair the seed. Do not expose internal checks or reasoning; no external retry/fallback is authorized.
